security_problem: A single MCP capability delegation call can be individually authorized while it activates authority for another principal or a transitive chain of principals outside the originating mandate. Every individual call can be credential-valid and policy-allowed while the system-wide authority graph still expands illegitimately.
required_behavior: Evaluate one proposed mcp_capability_delegation(grantor, grantee, capability) edge against the declared graph: ALLOW iff DirectOperationAuthorized AND Reach(G_after) is a subset of Mandate, with Reach(G_before) subset of Mandate enforced as a fail-closed precondition. Unknown principals/capabilities/action types, empty identifiers, and grantors lacking the delegated capability deny with stable reason codes and no fabricated authority result. Every receipt is deterministic with lexicographically sorted authority-pair arrays.
failure_behavior: Fail closed: invalid baseline, unknown references, malformed action type, or grantor without capability produce a deny receipt with a stable reason code and no fabricated authority result; unreadable or malformed request JSON exits non-zero with no partial JSON receipt on stdout.
